item.meaning: The constitutional right of every adult citizen aged 18+ to cast one vote of equal value in elections.
item.source_context: Chapter 9 & 10: Types of Governments & The Constitution

item.definition: A form of government where power is concentrated in the hands of a small, wealthy, or privileged elite group.
item.source_context: Chapter 9: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments

item.description: The division of state authority among Legislative, Executive, and Judicial branches to establish checks and balances against tyranny.

categories: Democracy (Direct vs Representative / Parliamentary vs Presidential)
Oligarchy (Rule by a small wealthy elite)
item.source_context: Chapter 9: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments

categories: Legislature: Law-making elected assembly (Parliament / State Assembly)
Executive: Law-enforcing administration (Prime Minister, Cabinet, Civil Services)
Judiciary: Law-interpreting independent courts (Supreme Court, High Courts)

item.significance: Inter-institutional oversight where Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary prevent any single branch from abusing power.
